notes: **New shipped procedure `gator-version-drift.md`** (roadmap Current Priority #5 deliverable) — written in `templates/gator-starter/procedures/` and copied to this repo's `.gator/.includes/procedures/`. Gives agents full self-sufficiency on `.gator/` merge conflicts and cross-branch version skew, with the operator never consulted on routine resolution. Core principle: shipped content is generated and version-owned — take either side whole, then `gator update` re-canonicalizes; user-authored knowledge merges as real prose with per-file semantics (inbox = union of open items; roadmap = more-advanced status wins; charters = must describe the MERGED code, verify via charter-alignment); session snippets = union both sides, never delete. Five scenario walkthroughs (merge across an update, coexisting versions with no merge planned = do nothing, origin ahead, origin behind, `.gator-version` conflicts), a what-NOT-to-do list, and the failure-modes-without-this section.

**Discovered + fixed a real propagation gap**: the v2.7.0 "shipped procedures" (`committing-gator-files.md`, `pre-gator-residue.md`) existed only in this repo's `.gator/.includes/` — never in `templates/gator-starter/procedures/` — so `gator update` never propagated them to fleet repos, contradicting the v2.7.0 release claim. Both backfilled into the template verbatim (files inside `SHIPPED_TEMPLATE_DIRS` directories propagate automatically; no constant change needed).
